question: Who studied ecological succession in the Indiana Dunes of Northwest Indiana in the 1890s?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry Chandler Cowles**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Henry Chandler Cowles** studied **ecological succession **in the **Indiana Dunes of Northwest Indiana in the 1890s**.
 
• **Henry Chandler Cowles (1869-1939)** was a **University of Chicago botany professor and conservationist**, his **studies of plant life in the Indiana Dunes made Cowles one of America's most notable early ecologists**.
 
• In **1896, Cowles** traveled to the southern shore of **Lake Michigan to see the Indiana Dunes **for the first time and studied them.
 
• His study explained the **development and distribution of local plant communities in terms of topography, moisture, wind, erosion, sedimentation, and other geological processes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **G Evelyn Hutchinson **was a British ecologist sometimes described as the **"father of modern ecology".**
 
• **Frederic Clements** was an American botanist, taxonomist, and ecologist who influenced the early study of plant communities, particularly the process of plant succession.
 
• **Charles Sutherland Elton FRS **was an English zoologist and animal ecologist associated with the development of population and community ecology, including studies of invasive organisms.
